title: Cost Drill CSV Exporter and Role-Aware Attribution UI
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and prototype a first-class drilldown and export experience for token-level cost attribution targeted at finance and platform engineers. This ticket scopes a role-aware UI that surfaces per-message / per-token cost breakdowns, contextual grouping (by team, route, model, and customer), and an opinionated CSV/Parquet export template. The goal is to enable: 1) rapid investigation of cost anomalies, 2) shareable exports for chargeback and ledger ingestion, and 3) a compact pricing-preview that shows how slab/volume discounts and quantization profiles change unit costs. Design deliverables: annotated wireframes, Figma prototype, export schema spec, accessibility pass, and a short usability session with two finance customers.
acceptance_criteria: UI shows token-level cost rows with columns: timestamp, request_id, route, model_variant, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_unit_price, subtotal, attribution_tag(s), user_team, environment
Role-aware views: Platform Admin sees team and customer grouping; Finance sees chargeback-ready view (anonymized PII); Developer sees per-route and per-model breakdown
Export formats: CSV and Parquet templates defined with header mapping and sample file (<= 50k rows in prototype)
Pricing preview: interactive control to toggle slab and quantization presets and a real-time delta preview of total cost
Design documented with Figma link, annotated handoff notes, accessibility contrast checks, and edge-case states (empty, partial data, sampling)
decisions: Use compact row-first layout for heavy tables to optimize vertical scan and allow sticky column for request_id
Default export column set will be 'chargeback-ready' for Finance; users can select a compact or verbose template
Anonymization rules: PII fields will be hashed for finance exports unless 'include PII' permission is enabled for role
Pricing preview will apply same aggregation window as current dashboard (24h default) to keep expectations consistent
tradeoffs: Performance vs. fidelity: full per-token export is heavy; we will sample large datasets by default and provide a 'full export' asynchronous job for committed customers
UI density vs. learnability: packed tables increase information density for power users but require more microcopy and tooltips for occasional users
Immediate productization vs. long-term flexibility: implement two export schemas now (chargeback, audit) and leave schema extension for later releases
